paragraphs.title: The Psalm’s Heading and the Request for Shelter

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to show him?

easy.explanation: He says, “my soul trusteth in thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker say his soul trusts?

easy.explanation: He says, “in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge.”
easy.q: Where will the speaker take refuge?

medium.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the speaker’s earnest request for mercy.
medium.q: What does the repeated phrase “be merciful unto me” express?

medium.explanation: The image of shelter under wings represents God’s protection.
medium.q: What does “in the shadow of thy wings” suggest?

medium.explanation: He asks for refuge “until these calamities be overpast.”
medium.q: How long does the speaker seek refuge?

answers: Because the speaker trusts God, he seeks shelter in Him
Because the speaker fears God, he hides from Him
Because the speaker has defeated his enemies, he leaves God
challenge.explanation: His trust in God leads him to seek protection under God’s wings.
challenge.q: How do verses 1–2 connect trust with refuge?

answers: The speaker is facing serious trouble
The speaker is celebrating a harvest
The speaker is preparing a musical performance
challenge.explanation: The word refers to severe troubles from which he seeks protection.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the word “calamities”?

answers: Appeal for mercy, expression of trust, and request for shelter
challenge.explanation: The speaker first asks for mercy, declares trust, and requests refuge.
challenge.q: Which movement of thought appears in this passage?

paragraphs.title: A Call to the God of Rescue and Kindness

easy.explanation: He says, “I will cry unto God most high.”
easy.q: To whom will the speaker cry?

easy.explanation: God is described as the One “that performeth all things for me.”
easy.q: What does God perform for the speaker?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “God shall send forth his mercy and his truth.”
easy.q: What will God send from heaven?

answers: God is able to complete His work on the speaker’s behalf
God is preparing a feast for the nations
God is hiding from the speaker
medium.explanation: The phrase presents God as the One who acts and completes what is needed for him.
medium.q: What does “performeth all things for me” communicate?

answers: To save the speaker from his reproachful enemy
medium.explanation: The verse says that God will send from heaven and save him from the one who would swallow him up.
medium.q: What is the purpose of God’s sending help from heaven?

answers: They are presented as divine help
They are described as weapons of the enemy
They prevent the speaker from praying
medium.explanation: God’s mercy and truth are named as the means by which help comes.
medium.q: How are mercy and truth related to the speaker’s hope?

answers: The speaker faces an enemy but expects God’s saving help
The speaker celebrates victory but refuses to praise God
The speaker fears the heavens but trusts his enemies
challenge.explanation: Although an enemy threatens him, the speaker looks to God for rescue.
challenge.q: What contrast is found in this passage?

answers: It emphasizes God’s supreme authority and ability to help
It identifies the speaker’s enemies as rulers
It refers to the height of the cave
challenge.explanation: Calling God “most high” highlights His exalted power over the speaker’s trouble.
challenge.q: Why is the title “God most high” significant in context?

answers: It moves from calling on God to describing the danger from which he needs rescue
It moves from praise to a description of musical instruments
It moves from safety to a promise to attack others
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the appeal to God and then identifies the threatening situation.
challenge.q: How does the passage develop from verse 3 to verse 4?

paragraphs.title: The Danger of the Enemies and Their Downfall

easy.explanation: He says, “My soul is among lions.”
easy.q: Among what does the speaker’s soul find itself?

easy.explanation: Their teeth are described as “spears and arrows.”
easy.q: What are the enemies’ teeth compared to?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “They have prepared a net for my steps.”
easy.q: What did the enemies prepare for the speaker’s steps?

answers: The enemies are dangerous and predatory
The enemies are peaceful and harmless
medium.explanation: Lions represent the threatening and aggressive character of the enemies.
medium.q: What does the image of lions communicate?

answers: The destructive power of the enemies’ words
medium.explanation: The image shows that the enemies’ speech can wound like a weapon.
medium.q: What does the comparison of the tongue to a sharp sword emphasize?

answers: The speaker filled it with water
It became a place of refuge
medium.explanation: The verse says they “are fallen themselves” into the pit.
medium.q: What happened to the pit prepared by the enemies?

answers: They suffer through the trap they prepared for another
challenge.explanation: The enemies fall into the very pit they dug for the speaker.
challenge.q: What principle is illustrated by the enemies’ fall?

answers: From predatory enemies, to weapons of speech, to a failed trap
From celebration, to music, to sunrise
From refuge, to mercy, to heavenly praise
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the enemies’ character to their weapons and finally to their downfall.
challenge.q: How does the description of danger progress?

answers: The enemies threaten through both words and actions
The enemies are preparing a worship service
The enemies intend to protect the speaker
challenge.explanation: The images portray verbal attacks, physical danger, and deliberate plotting.
challenge.q: What does the combination of teeth, tongue, net, and pit reveal?

easy.q: What is the condition of the speaker’s heart?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will sing and give praise.”
easy.q: What will the speaker do with his fixed heart?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “awake, psaltery and harp.”
easy.q: Which instruments are told to awaken?

answers: The speaker is resolved and prepared to praise
The speaker has lost all courage
medium.explanation: A fixed heart indicates firmness and readiness.
medium.q: What does “my heart is fixed” suggest?

medium.explanation: The speaker calls himself and his instruments to awaken for worship.
medium.q: What does “Awake up, my glory” most likely mean in context?

answers: A steadfast heart leads to singing and praise
The music causes him to abandon trust
The heart and music are unrelated
medium.explanation: His fixed heart is followed by his resolve to sing and give praise.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the speaker’s heart and his music?

answers: The speaker turns from danger to determined praise
challenge.explanation: After describing danger, he declares that his heart is fixed and ready to praise.
challenge.q: What change occurs after the description of the enemies?

answers: The speaker intends to begin praising at the earliest time
The speaker plans to sleep through the danger
The speaker will wait for the enemies to sing
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses eagerness to awaken and praise early.
challenge.q: What does “I myself will awake early” indicate?

answers: They are poetically summoned to join the act of praise
They are being used to set a trap
challenge.explanation: The psalm personifies the instruments as participants in the coming praise.
challenge.q: Why are the instruments addressed directly?

paragraphs.title: Praise Among the Nations and the Greatness of Divine Kindness

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people.”
easy.q: Among whom will the speaker praise the Lord?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will sing unto thee among the nations.”
easy.q: Among whom will the speaker sing?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “For thy mercy is great unto the heavens.”

medium.explanation: He says, “thy truth unto the clouds.”
medium.q: Where does the speaker say God’s truth reaches?

answers: The praise is intended to be public and widely known
The praise is limited to the speaker’s household
medium.explanation: The people and nations represent a broad audience for the speaker’s worship.
medium.q: What does praising God among the nations suggest?

medium.explanation: The refrain repeats, “Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens.”
medium.q: What command is repeated in the closing refrain?

answers: It reaches from the individual speaker to peoples and nations
It narrows from nations to one enemy
It changes from praise to concealment
challenge.explanation: The speaker promises to praise God among both the people and the nations.
challenge.q: How does the scope of praise expand in this passage?

answers: Both are described as immense and extending beyond the earth
Both are presented as weapons of the enemies
Both are limited to the speaker’s refuge
challenge.explanation: Mercy reaches the heavens and truth reaches the clouds, showing their vastness.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between God’s mercy and truth?

answers: It emphasizes God’s exaltation and universal glory
It returns the poem to the enemies’ trap
challenge.explanation: The repetition gives the psalm a strong conclusion centered on God’s exaltation and glory.
challenge.q: What is the effect of the repeated final refrain?
